changelog.body:
Skips 4.8 — this release contains it.

**Google Photos Locked Folder works again on a device that really has a device owner, and without putting Photos in the scope.** The device-wide device-owner spoof now covers what apps actually read, not just the owner's name. It answers apps only; the framework asking itself still gets the truth.

Also since 4.7: app-facing categories run only in apps you scope, unknown-sources session installs and uninstalls go through, and the module switches itself off instead of defaulting everything on if it cannot read its own settings.

Reported and verified by @MootComb.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/DuckDevicePolicy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

**Fixes a bootloop. Update if you are on 4.3 - 4.6 and your device really has a device owner or a work profile.**

The ownership checks added in 4.3 were also answering system_server's own questions, not just apps'. On a device that genuinely is managed, `DevicePolicyManagerService` asks about device-owner state on the boot path, got the spoofed answer, and threw at PHASE_LOCK_SETTINGS_READY — taking system_server down in a loop.

Ownership answers now go to apps only; the framework asking itself gets the truth.

If you are stuck in the loop: disable the module (or Zygisk) from your root manager, or `adb uninstall com.strawing.duckdevicepolicy` while it restarts.

Reported by @MootComb.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/DuckDevicePolicy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

The Diagnostics tab said it showed the real restriction values. It doesn't, and it now says so: the app asks the same way any app asks, and the answer comes from system_server, which is where the device-wide hooks live. With those categories on, a key reads "not set" whether it was never set or the bypass is clearing it. `adb shell dumpsys user` is the unfiltered truth.

Long restriction keys wrap on the underscores instead of splitting mid-word.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/DuckDevicePolicy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

The Diagnostics tab now shows which restrictions your device actually has — read live, outside the module scope, so they are the real values and not what the hooks show other apps — instead of an empty report that was never going to arrive.

It also says plainly where the hook report is: the LSPosed log. The framework's file store for a module is root-owned, so a hooked process cannot write into it and that screen has no way to receive one. Look for `installed N/M hooks in <process>` and `first hit: <category>`.

If you are coming from 4.3 or earlier, 4.4 is the important one: the device-wide categories only worked if you ticked the framework scope entry that actually reaches system_server, and managers disagree about whether that is `android`, `system` or `system_server`. Tick every one your manager offers.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/DuckDevicePolicy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Renamed to DuckDevicePolicy in 4.2 (same package, updates in place, settings and scope kept) and rebuilt the UI: Status / Categories / Diagnostics tabs, with categories split into device-wide and app-facing.

4.3 adds **Device-owner / fully-managed checks** — hides `getDeviceOwner`, `getDeviceOwnerComponentOnAnyUser`, `getActiveAdmins`, `getProfileOwner*` and friends. That is what an app reads before refusing a feature because the device is "fully managed" (Google Photos' Locked Folder is the usual one). The app must be in the module scope. A device-wide variant hooking `DevicePolicyManagerService` is included but **off by default**.

It also says what it did. Every build now logs `installed N/M hooks in <process>`, names every row it could not resolve, and logs the first time each category actually fires. Please quote those lines when reporting a problem.

Reminder: the install / uninstall and developer-options categories need **System Framework** (`android`) in the scope; from an app's scope they cannot work.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/FuckDevicePolicy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Restores sideloading APKs from normal apps (Telegram, browsers, file managers) when a work profile or MDM blocks it, and the developer-options / USB-debugging block.

Two new categories, both on by default, hook `com.android.server.pm.UserManagerService` inside system_server rather than only the client-side `android.os.UserManager` wrapper — the service is where the refusal is actually decided, including in the package-installer process the module is not scoped into.

Requires System Framework (`android`) scope for those two categories. Settings and scope carry over from 4.0.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/FuckDevicePolicy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Migrated to the modern Xposed API (libxposed).

**Requires an LSPosed 2.x fork** implementing modern API 101+ (`minApiVersion=101` / `targetApiVersion=102`). Mainline LSPosed 1.9.x will not load this build — stay on 3.1 there.

- Entry points now declared in `META-INF/xposed/`; `onSystemServerStarting` + `onPackageReady` replace `handleLoadPackage`.
- Settings moved off `XSharedPreferences` to framework remote preferences: toggles apply live, no reboot. The app can now read and show its own LSPosed scope.
- Outlook enrollment-gate hooks install only in Outlook's process.
- Your scope is preserved on upgrade; **3.x settings are not** — you start from defaults (everything on).
- minSdk 21 -> 26.

Full changelog: https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/FuckDevicePolicy/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Adds an Outlook enrollment-gate category (hooks Outlook's own DevicePolicy.requiresDeviceManagement/isPolicyApplied) alongside the existing DevicePolicyManager/UserManager coverage. See https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/FuckDevicePolicy/releases/tag/v3.1 for full changelog.

v3.0 — full Kotlin rewrite

A ground-up rewrite (fork of liyafe1997/FuckDevicePolicy) that turns the module
from a single UserManager patch into a per-category DevicePolicyManager +
UserManager bypass with a real UI.

Highlights
- New Material You UI: master toggle, per-category switches, All / None quick actions.
- Coverage expanded from UserManager-only to 12 categories across
  DevicePolicyManager AND UserManager:
  camera block · screenshot/screen-record block · device admin & owner checks ·
  password & PIN policy · lock-screen (keyguard) feature limits ·
  storage-encryption enforcement · managed app configuration ·
  user restrictions (DISALLOW_*, incl. UserManager.hasUserRestriction) ·
  auto-lock timeout · kiosk / lock-task mode · permitted IMEs & accessibility ·
  misc (auto-time, cross-profile, Bluetooth …).
- Settings shared cross-process via XSharedPreferences (per-hook try/catch,
  hook-once-per-process).
- Material You dynamic colours (Android 12+) and a new adaptive icon.
- Signed release, R8 + resource shrinking (~1.8 MB).

Scope
- Recommended: System Framework (android) for system-wide effect.
- Do NOT scope the MDM app itself (Intune / Company Portal).
- Enable + reboot once before relying on the toggles (cross-process prefs).

Notes
- Client-side hooks change what apps/framework SEE, not what system_server
  enforces. For your own device.

changelog.name: DuckDevicePolicy
changelog.body:
Bypass Intune Restrictions

This module can let you make some user restriction policies (set by Device Admin App or Work Profile, e.g. Microsoft Intune) nonfunctional. Especially some device-wide policies, even it is in the Work Profile but affected the outside whole android environment(Your Personal Profile).

简体中文 (Simplified Chinese) 该模块可以让一些Android的用户限制策略失效，这些策略一般由“设备管理员”App设置，或者“工作配置文件”。比如Microsoft Intune（又叫“公司门户”）就是用来干这事的。特别是一些全局策略，即使是在工作配置文件里面设置的，但是会影响到外面的整个安卓（你的个人空间，即安卓的主环境）

![494123554-e94cf8e6-b228-413a-98b6-0ae6de232326](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9dd0898-5ef9-4429-b4cd-7ae10d65b1da)


https://github.com/Xposed-Modules-Repo/com.strawing.duckdevicepolicy

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/Xposed-Modules-Repo/com.strawing.duckdevicepolicy/commits/2-2.0

readme: # DuckDevicePolicy Makes apps see **no device-policy restrictions** on your own device — `DevicePolicyManager` / `UserManager` checks answered "no restriction", per category, behind a master toggle. Formerly DuckPolicy, same package, so it updates in place and keeps your settings and scope. **Needs an LSPosed 2.x fork** (Xposed API 101+). Mainline 1.9.x will not load it. **Scope matters.** Tick every framework entry your manager offers — `android`, `system`, `system_server`. They disagree about which one actually reaches system_server, and the wrong one silently does nothing. That covers the device-wide categories: app install / uninstall, developer options, device-owner spoof. The target app for everything else, including the device-owner checks Google Photos reads for Locked Folder. Never scope Intune / Company Portal / Authenticator. **Not working?** The LSPosed log has `installed N/M hooks in `, which names anything that did not resolve, and `first hit: ...` the first time one fires. Quote both when reporting. Source & issues: **https://github.com/Bouteillepleine/DuckDevicePolicy** · fork of [liyafe1997/FuckDevicePolicy](https://github.com/liyafe1997/FuckDevicePolicy). --- ### 简体中文 让 App 在你自己的设备上看到「没有任何设备策略限制」，按类别挂钩 `DevicePolicyManager` / `UserManager` 的检查并返回「无限制」，带总开关。 原名 DuckPolicy，包名不变，可直接覆盖升级。**需要 LSPosed 2.x 分支**（Xposed API 101+）。 作用域决定能否生效：请把管理器提供的**所有框架条目**都勾上——`android`、`system`、 `system_server`，不同管理器对「哪一个真正进入 system_server」并不一致，勾错的那个不会有任何效果。 它们对应全设备类别（应用安装/卸载、开发者选项、设备所有者伪装）；**目标应用** 用于其余类别， 包括 Google 相册锁定文件夹读取的「设备所有者 / 完全托管检查」。 请勿将 Intune / 公司门户 / Authenticator 加入作用域。 反馈问题时请附上 LSPosed 日志中的 `installed N/M hooks in <进程>` 与 `first hit:` 两行。
